thread:
opsbot: INCIDENT P1 - Cascade Enterprise (private VPC / dedicated pool) - observed partial egress blackhole to external services, alerting from healthchecks and customer page
opsbot: Pager: @lex oncall, channel: #incidents, severity: P1, links: https://incidents.example/1942106789
lex: seeing the alert, jumping in. any immediate customer impact notes?
owen: customer reports some downstream APIs failing (payment gateway + telemetry sinks), roughly 10% of requests hitting 502 / connection timeout, started ~22:12 UTC
maya: I can access the customer's VPC console. quick summary: dedicated pool nodes in us-east-1 are showing high conntrack and a mix of ECONNRESET to external IP ranges used by payment gateway. NLB healthchecks for the ALB targets are flapping.
lex: ok. first step: are we sure this is networking at infra level and not the app? any increase in 5xx from the app?
maya: app logs show normal processing until socket write fails. stack traces show network-level resets. traceroute from node -> payment gateway stops at our NAT path.
lex: sounds like egress path. infra-bot, any recent churn to security groups or NACLs for Cascade's VPC?
infra-bot: Automation run: sg-auto-remediate job executed at 22:08 UTC for orphaned rules across tenants. Target: cascade-private-sg-123. Change: removed wide ephemeral allow 1024-65535 for cross-az LB healthcheck IPs.
lex: that matches timeline. so auto-remediate tightened the SG and likely blocked connections used by NAT / LB healthchecks. maya, can you confirm the exact rule removal?
maya: confirmed: sg rule id r-0abcd removed: tcp 1024-65535 from 10.0.0.0/8. healthchecks originate from 10.0.5.12 (internal LB IP) on high port 54123 -> were being accepted before.
lex: immediate mitigation: add a temporary allow for healthcheck IPs + ephemeral range, and exempt Cascade's SG from auto-remediate. who can apply a hotspot rule?
maya: I can push. applying a very focused rule: allow tcp 1024-65535 from 10.0.5.0/24 to cascade-private-sg-123. doing it now.
maya: rule added. checking connectivity…
maya: NLB healthchecks recovering on 3 of 4 AZs, connection failures dropping. 502 rate down to 2% now.
lex: nice. keep monitoring. what's the mitigation window — we need to keep this temporary rule at least until we patch automation.
owen: told customer we're doing a short mitigation; they're asking for ETA and whether this is customer-isolated.
lex: short answer: it's caused by our automation mistakenly flagging a shared ephemeral rule as orphaned; limited to tenants with that security layout. Cascade impacted because their dedicated pool uses cross-az NLB healthchecks from internal IP range.
lex: Ria, can you triage security exposure of leaving ephemeral allow in place?
ria: brief check: the temporary rule restricts source to 10.0.5.0/24 only. attacker needs internal placement to exploit. low risk for external attack, acceptable for short RTO. I recommend we rotate to a narrower allow: only known LB IDs' IPs + document exception.
lex: agreed. next: automation fix. infra-bot, can you pause sg-auto-remediate globally or whitelist Cascade?
infra-bot: sg-auto-remediate paused for affected account(s) at 22:30 UTC. whitelist entry created: cascade-account-id.
lex: good. follow-up: we need a permanent change to automation to avoid removing ephemeral ranges that are referenced by load balancers / NAT. Maya, can you own a patch?
maya: will open PR to change logic: check for reference from ELB/NLB/ENI before removal and add a 7-day grace for ephemeral ports. starting work now.
lex: deploy-bot, can you run a canary to test PR once ready?
deploy-bot: noted. will run staged canary on staging automation at 23:45 UTC once PR merged.
lex: routing fallback: can we fail traffic to the dedicated pool to a regional standby pool if this recurs?
maya: we have a hot standby in us-east-2 but DNS/route change currently manual; we can initiate a traffic shift via routing policy but need CS approval. Owen, can you coordinate with the customer?
owen: Cascade is nervous but wants us to prioritize fixing automation first. They don't want emergency failover unless prolonged. I'll advise them of current mitigation and the pause.
lex: good. monitoring: set up short-live synthetic checks to the payment gateway via Cascade pool every 30s and alert if >5% failures for 5m. opsbot, create alert.
opsbot: alert rule created: cascade-private-egress-synthetics, threshold 5% over 5m, notify #incidents and @lex.
maya: further check: conntrack table was near capacity on some nodes which contributed to drops. increasing conntrack max on impacted nodes as stopgap. doing now.
maya: conntrack bump applied, no adverse effects. combined SG rule + conntrack bump restored stable egress for now. 200 OK rate ~99.6% over last 10m.
lex: timeline for permanent fixes? maya: PR drafted, will run review today, aim to merge + deploy to automation by 48h. infra will add whitelist UI for enterprise customers within 72h.
ria: I'll write a short security risk note and sign off on temporary exception.
owen: customer notified, thanked us for quick action, asked for postmortem + RCA. they'll expect an executive summary.
lex: assign postmortem to ops lead + eng-automation. I'll own the incident doc. tagging follow-ups: ACTIONS: 1) patch sg-auto-remediate (maya) 2) whitelist UI + admin control (infra) 3) postmortem + exec summary (lex) 4) update runbook for dedicated pools + LB healthchecks (owen)
opsbot: Incident marked RESOLVED at 23:03 UTC after sustained recovery and customer confirmation.
lex: handing off to oncall 2 for watch. @maya @ria @owen — please add any notes to the incident doc.
deploy-bot: automation canary scheduled for 23:45 UTC. will report results in this thread.
infra-bot: NOTE: we found 2 other tenants with similar SG patterns; we reached out to their owners to confirm. no active impact observed.
deploy-bot: canary complete: staging automation passed smoke tests. rollback not required. will schedule prod deploy 48h after review window.
lex: thanks team. I'll convert this thread into the postmortem skeleton and ping for timelines. closing channel for active paging.
maya: adding config snippets to PR and adding exact sg rule IDs to incident doc.
ria: will include recommended security posture for exceptions.
owen: customer asked for timestamped timeline; I'll add their quotes to the postmortem.
lex: good work. incident closed, follow-ups tracked. :thumbsup:
